content.title: Hawks vs. Rockets: Prediction, How to Watch for Free (3/20/26)
content.text: The Atlanta Hawks (38–31) face the Houston Rockets (41–27) tonight at Toyota Center in Houston. The Hawks continue to soar, entering tonight on an 11-game winning streak. They now sit in sixth place in the Eastern Conference, currently holding the final automatic playoff spot. On Wednesday, Atlanta defeated the Dallas Mavericks 135–120, topping the 120-point mark for the third straight game. CJ McCollum led the way with 24 points on 9-of-14 shooting, while Nickeil Alexander-Walker followed with 22. Jalen Johnson added 17 points and 11 rebounds, once again flirting with a triple-double, finishing just one assist short. Another recent addition, Jonathan Kuminga, provided an efficient burst off the bench, scoring 16 points in just 18 minutes. Despite the roster changes, Atlanta is once again showcasing the same balanced, high-efficiency scoring that defined its early-season success before a midseason slide. Now, the Hawks are peaking at the right time. The Rockets, meanwhile, have dropped two straight and six of their last 10 games. They were swept in a two-game home set by the Los Angeles Lakers, losing both contests by eight points. On Wednesday, Houston had no answer for the Luka Doncic–LeBron James tandem, which combined for 70 points. James was nearly flawless from the field, hitting 13 of 14 attempts, as the Lakers shot 61% overall — a clear indictment of Houston’s defensive struggles. Offensively, the Rockets displayed similar balance. Alperen Sengun led with 27 points, while Amen Thompson added 26. Houston held a 109–107 lead with just over four minutes remaining before the Lakers closed the game on a decisive 15–7 run. Despite the recent slump, the Rockets remain in fifth place in the Western Conference, though they sit 13 games out of first. With several teams around them also hovering around .500 over their last 10 games, Houston has been able to maintain its position — even while playing below its best level. The Rockets are struggling against top-tier opponents. Expect that to continue tonight as the Hawks’ scoring balance proves too much for them to handle. Prediction: Atlanta Hawks 121, Houston Rockets 115 Injury Report Atlanta Hawks Jonathan Kuminga — Out (Knee) Houston Rockets Jae’Sean Tate — Out (Knee) Steven Adams — Out For Season (Ankle) Fred VanVleet — Out (Knee) How to Watch Hawks vs. Rockets Tip-off for tonight’s Hawks-Rockets game is set for 8:00 PM Eastern / 7:00 PM Central at the Toyota Center in Houston.
